def-emg-geometric-scaling:
## Definition

Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and arbitrary smooth real two-form $F$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. In a chart using the coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ with all four coordinates assigned metres, assign the SI component unit tesla to $F_{ab}$; the two-form $F=\frac12F_{ab}\,dx^a\wedge dx^b$ then has unit weber.

For this conversion dictionary, take $c>0$, $G>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ as numerical input parameters, with SI dimensions

$$[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\qquad [G]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}},\qquad [\mu_0]=\mathrm{kg\,m\,C^{-2}}.$$

Define the derived parameters

$$\varepsilon_0:=\frac{1}{\mu_0c^2},\qquad \kappa:=\frac{8\pi G}{c^4},\qquad \alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{\kappa}{2\mu_0}},\qquad \mathcal F:=\alpha F.$$

Thus $\varepsilon_0$ has unit $\mathrm{C^2\,s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\kappa$ has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$, $\alpha$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,s\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and the components $\mathcal F_{ab}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. In modern SI, $c$ is fixed exactly by the definition of the metre; $\mu_0$ is not fixed exactly and its numerical value is determined experimentally. Here the equations use only the positive symbolic parameters above, not a selected numerical value.

For a physical mass $M_{\!p}>0$ in kilograms, signed charge $Q_e$ in coulombs, and angular momentum $J_{\mathrm{ang}}$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$, define the geometric length parameters

$$m_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\frac{GM_{\!p}}{c^2},\qquad q_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\sqrt{\frac{G}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad a_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\frac{J_{\mathrm{ang}}}{M_{\!p}c}.$$

For a supplied magnetic-flux parameter $\Phi_B$ in webers, also define $p_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\alpha\Phi_B/(4\pi)$ in metres. This is only a conversion of an already specified flux value; it asserts neither a global potential nor a magnetic source. The inverse parameter maps are $M_{\!p}=c^2m_{\mathrm{geo}}/G$, $Q_e=\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4/G}\,q_{\mathrm{geo}}$, $J_{\mathrm{ang}}=M_{\!p}c\,a_{\mathrm{geo}}$, and $\Phi_B=4\pi p_{\mathrm{geo}}/\alpha$.

The mass, charge, angular momentum and flux are inputs to this dictionary; their primitive or derived status in any physical model is framework-specific. No field equation, Maxwell postulate, matter law, or empirical value is part of this definition.
thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N,o)$, $F$, $\kappa$, $\mu_0$, $\alpha$ and $\mathcal F=\alpha F$ be as in [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]], with curvature tensors defined by [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant. Define the quadratic tensor

$$\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},$$

where indices are raised with $g^{-1}$. Then the following equations for the same metric and two-form are equivalent:

$$G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),$$

$$G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=2\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F),$$

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g)-\Lambda g_{ab}=2\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F).$$

These are algebraic equivalences between tensor equations. No Maxwell equation, matter model, limiting procedure or physical solution is assumed.
thm-emg-conformal-maxwell:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ and a smooth real two-form $F$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $\Omega:M\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth dimensionless function, put $\widetilde g=\Omega^2g$ with the same orientation, let $\mu_0>0$ be constant, and let $j$ be a smooth vector field. The Hodge operator is that of [[lem-emg-conformal-hodge-multiplier]]. Define

$$\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T_{ab}(g,F):=\mu_0^{-1}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Then $(F,j)$ satisfies the differential-form Maxwell equations

$$dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\,\iota_j\operatorname{vol}_g$$

if and only if $(F,\widetilde j)$ satisfies the same equations for $\widetilde g$, where $\widetilde j:=\Omega^{-4}j$. In addition,

$$\operatorname{vol}_{\widetilde g}=\Omega^4\operatorname{vol}_g,\qquad \iota_{\widetilde j}\operatorname{vol}_{\widetilde g}=\iota_j\operatorname{vol}_g,\qquad \widetilde T_{ab}=\Omega^{-2}T_{ab},\qquad \widetilde T^{ab}=\Omega^{-6}T^{ab}.$$

If $n$ is a $g$-unit timelike vector, then $\widetilde n:=\Omega^{-1}n$ is $\widetilde g$-unit timelike and $\widetilde T(\widetilde n,\widetilde n)=\Omega^{-4}T(n,n)$. On any oriented integration domain where the integral exists, or for a compactly supported action difference, the quadratic integral $\int F_{ab}F^{ab}\operatorname{vol}_g$ is unchanged. These are tensor identities; they do not assert Einstein-equation or matter-model invariance.
thm-emg-conformal-einstein-transformatio:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the curvature convention and tensors of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Let $\Omega:M\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth and dimensionless, and put $\widetilde g=\Omega^2g$ with the same orientation. Use the metric-selected connection and its tensor derivative of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Define the smooth one-form and its contractions by

$$u:=\Omega^{-1}d\Omega,\qquad H_{ab}:=(\nabla_a u)_b,\qquad \theta:=g^{ab}H_{ab},\qquad s:=g^{ab}u_au_b.$$

Then $H_{ab}=H_{ba}$ and

$$\widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-2H_{ab}-g_{ab}\theta+2u_au_b-2g_{ab}s,$$

$$\widetilde S=\Omega^{-2}(S-6\theta-6s),$$

$$\widetilde G_{ab}=G_{ab}-2H_{ab}+2u_au_b+2g_{ab}\theta+g_{ab}s.$$

All curvature conventions are those stated in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. These are mathematical transformation identities, not an assertion that the Einstein equation is conformally invariant.
prop-emg-constant-electrovac-rescaling:
## Statement

Let $g,F,j,\Lambda,c,G,\mu_0,\kappa$ be as in [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]] and the four-dimensional Lorentzian curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Suppose they satisfy the formal sourced Einstein–Maxwell equations

$$G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\,\iota_j\operatorname{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathcal Q$ is the quadratic tensor of [[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]]. For a positive dimensionless constant $\lambda$, define

$$g':=\lambda^2g,\qquad F':=\lambda F,\qquad \Lambda':=\lambda^{-2}\Lambda,\qquad j':=\lambda^{-3}j.$$

Then $(g',F',j',\Lambda')$ satisfies the same equations with the same numerical constants $c,G,\mu_0$. In particular, a source-free electrovac solution ($j=0$) maps to a source-free electrovac solution. No transformation law for an additional matter stress tensor or matter action is asserted.
prop-emg-test-field-residual-order:
## Statement

Let $U$ be a smooth Lorentzian four-dimensional chart domain with metric $g$ and constant $\Lambda$ as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Suppose $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$. Let $F_1$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$ satisfying $dF_1=0$ and $d(\star_gF_1)=0$. For any real dimensionless $\varepsilon$, put $F_\varepsilon:=\varepsilon F_1$ and define

$$T^{(1)}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F_1),\qquad \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),$$

using $\kappa,\mu_0,\mathcal Q$ of [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]] and [[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]]. Then $F_\varepsilon$ remains an exact source-free Maxwell field on the fixed metric and

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\varepsilon;\Lambda)=-\kappa\varepsilon^2T^{(1)}_{ab}.$$

For a compact set $K\subset U$, fix the chart component norm $\|S\|_{K}:=\max_{a,b}\sup_{p\in K}|S_{ab}(p)|$. It is finite for smooth $S$ and satisfies

$$\|\mathscr R(g,F_\varepsilon;\Lambda)\|_K=\kappa\varepsilon^2\|T^{(1)}\|_K.$$

If $\varepsilon\ne0$ and $T^{(1)}$ is not identically zero on $K$, the fixed pair $(g,F_\varepsilon)$ is not an exact coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution on $K$. This is a residual estimate only; it gives no nearby metric, solution-distance bound, point-source solution or backreaction limit.
